routes.label: Draw a diagonal to reveal familiar shapes

question: All sides of the convex pentagon \(ABCDE\) are of equal length, and \(\angle A = \angle B = 90^\circ.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle E?\)
solution:
Draw diagonal \(CE\). The two right angles suggest a square: both \(AE\) and \(BC\) are perpendicular to \(AB\), and convexity places \(E\) and \(C\) on the same side of \(AB\). Thus \(AE\parallel BC\). Since these opposite sides of quadrilateral \(ABCE\) are also equal, \(ABCE\) is a parallelogram. It has a right angle and equal adjacent sides \(AB=BC\), so it is a square.

Let the common pentagon side length be \(s\). The square gives \(CE=AB=s\), while the original conditions give \(CD=DE=s\). Hence triangle \(CDE\) is equilateral, so \(\angle CED=60^\circ\).

Because \(CE\) is a diagonal of the convex pentagon, it splits the interior angle at \(E\). Therefore
\[
\angle E=\angle AEC+\angle CED
=90^\circ+60^\circ=\boxed{150^\circ},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
